metadata.description: The Natchez, Jackson and Columbus ('Little J'), the 98-mile 3 ft 6 in gauge line Natchez - Fayette - Harriston - Pattison - Hermanville - Utica - Raymond - Jackson, Mississippi, drawn by operator era: the NJ&C's three staged sections (Natchez - Pattison from 1881, Pattison - Raymond from 1882, Raymond - Jackson from 1883) to 1889; the Louisville, New Orleans and Texas 1890-1891; and the Yazoo and Mississippi Valley (Illinois Central) 1892-1939. All five features share identical vertices. The never-built Jackson - Columbus extension is not drawn.
metadata.colour_normalization: Rule 4: Yazoo and Mississippi Valley #F4801F pulled programmatically from ymv_memphis_vicksburg.geojson's feature with company 'Yazoo and Mississippi Valley Railroad (Illinois Central)', company string reused verbatim. Natchez, Jackson and Columbus #2F6F6F and Louisville, New Orleans and Texas #8A3B5E are new: neither company had a colour or feature anywhere in data/, and both hexes were checked programmatically to be unused by any feature.
metadata.ownership_splits: 28 Mar 1890 NJ&C -> Louisville, New Orleans and Texas (sale; standard-gauge conversion); 1892 LNO&T -> Yazoo and Mississippi Valley (Illinois Central). The report's drawable spans share their boundary years (NJ&C to 1890, LNO&T 1890-1892, Y&MV from 1892); to avoid drawing the same track twice in one year, each transfer year is drawn only on the incoming operator's feature (NJ&C ends 1889, LNO&T 1890-1891, Y&MV from 1892). This narrows, never widens, the drawable spans. The 1946 Y&MV -> IC merger falls after the drawn end and is not a colour change in this repo.
omitted: Natchez - Pattison 1877/1879-1880: opening conflicting (Rowland 1876-77 vs msrailroads Jan 1879) and no passenger year confirmed before the 1881 Official Guide.
Pattison - Raymond before 1882 and Raymond - Jackson before 1883: opening dates not established / completion late 1882.
The unknown passenger years between ~1940 and 1951: no source dates the end; only freight-only status by 30 Sep 1951 is proven.
Freight-only years to the 1979-81 ICG abandonment and the CN Natchez stub 1998-2005 (Rule 1).
not_yet_sourced: PASSENGER END of the Y&MV/IC Natchez - Jackson service: 1939 is an [OPEN] last-implied year from one secondary undated statement ('until early 1940's', chicagorailfan.com); primary evidence only proves freight-only by 30 Sep 1951 (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 80). Next sources: an IC public timetable 1937-1945, Mississippi Railroad Commission discontinuance orders, a Natchez Democrat 'last train' story.
No dated passenger timetable at all for 1890-1939 (LNO&T and Y&MV eras); both spans rest on continuity and ownership dates.

[OPEN] starts: NJ&C Natchez - Pattison 1881 (first Official Guide evidence), Pattison - Raymond 1882 (June 1882 newspapers), Raymond - Jackson 1883 (completion late 1882; no timetable before 1889 seen; msrailroads' 1885 Guide image not inspected).
Headway and speed for every era are estimates.
Date of the LNO&T standard-gauge conversion; whether it or later IC work moved the alignment drawn.
source_conflicts: Opening of Natchez - Martin (Pattison): msrailroads January 1879 vs Rowland 1876-77.
Completion to Jackson: msrailroads 14 Sep 1882 vs Rowland 6 Oct 1882.
Charter: msrailroads text 1870 vs its header 1873.
Martin: branchline identifies Martin with Pattison (MP 42.7, used here); icrr.net also lists a separate 'Martin' at its MP 48.0.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Rule 1 applied at creation: nothing drawn after 1939; the freight-only years to 1979-81 and the CN-era Natchez stub are excluded.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Rule 5: steam from opening; nothing to exclude.
metadata.interurban_audit: Rule 7: steam railroad, intercity_rail; no interurban.

properties.line: Natchez, Jackson and Columbus: Natchez – Pattison
properties.speed_source: estimated: no running time found for any era; a typical figure for a 3 ft 6 in Southern narrow-gauge steam road of the 1880s. NOT sourced.
properties.geometry_source: Traced with opstrace.py over OpenStreetMap (Overpass, maps.mail.ru mirror) plus OpenHistoricalMap. Preferred at 1x: OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=IC (here almost all railway=abandoned: way 791484200 Natchez - Stampley and way 13608727 Stampley - west edge of Jackson) and the OHM way 201241436 (operator 'Natchez, Jackson and Columbus Railroad', Hermanville - Jackson); the router took the OHM way Hermanville - Jackson, which lies within 150 m of the OSM abandoned grade everywhere the two overlap. The whole Natchez - Jackson line was traced in one pass and cut at Pattison and Raymond (points projected onto the line), so all five features share identical vertices. Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed; no out-and-back spurs.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced end to end, no straight-line leg: 42.1 mi drawn vs 42.7 mi (branchline SL246 MP 0.0 - 42.7; msrailroads '43 miles') documented Natchez - Pattison (Martin). Cut at Pattison 156 m from its geocode. Waypoints Natchez 0.5 km, Washington 2.7 km (the railroad passed Washington at Selma / Washington Crossing, not through the village), Stanton 0.0, Stampley 0.0, Fayette 0.4, Harriston 0.1, Red Lick 0.3, Pattison 0.2, Hermanville 0.0, Carlisle 0.0, Utica 0.0, Learned 0.1, Raymond 0.1, McRaven 0.1, Jackson (IC depot, hand-pinned) 0.0 km from the line. LATER ALIGNMENT: the grade drawn is the one the Illinois Central abandoned in 1979-81, i.e. as it stood after the LNO&T's conversion from 3 ft 6 in to standard gauge (date not found). Whether conversion or later IC work relocated any part of the original narrow-gauge alignment has NOT been checked. The Natchez terminal is where the OSM IC grade ends at Monroe St (31.5616 N, 91.3975 W); the NJ&C's own Natchez depot site is not pinned. The Jackson end is the IC depot (the OHM way ends ~150 m south of it; the last 0.1 mi is on today's CN McComb Subdivision).

segments.note: The NJ&C's first section, Natchez - Washington Crossing (Selma) - Stanton - Cannonsburg - Fayette - Harriston - Pattison (the 1879 railhead 'Martin' / 'Martins'), 3 ft 6 in gauge (Weekly Copiahan 24 Jun 1882; msrailroads). [OPEN] START: 1881 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year, not the opening - the 1881 Official Guide carries the stations' former names Brandon (Stanton) and Greenwood (Cannonsburg) (branchline SL246 '1881G'). SOURCE CONFLICT on the opening, recorded not resolved: msrailroads 'opened January 1879, Natchez to Martins'; Rowland's Encyclopedia 'built to Martin in 1876-77'. 1877-1880 are unproven and not drawn; do not move the start earlier without a dated timetable or newspaper. END: the NJ&C was sold to the Louisville, New Orleans and Texas on 28 Mar 1890 - an ownership end, not a service end; last direct NJ&C-era evidence is the 1889 equipment list (msrailroads, indirect). The report's drawable span runs to 1890; 1890 is drawn on the LNO&T feature instead so no year is drawn twice on the same track. headway_min 720 (two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE: no timetable frequency was read for any era; the 1889 roster (4 coaches, 2 combines) is consistent with one or two round trips a day.
sources: Segment-level: start 1881 from the 1881 Official Guide name notes in branchline SL246 line 31; opening conflict (1879 msrailroads vs 1876-77 Rowland) recorded in the note; end from the 28 Mar 1890 sale (msrailroads). Headway NOT sourced.
https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/mississippirrs.pdf (SL246 'Mississippi Railroads' passenger station guide, line 31: Natchez - Jackson mileposts and Official Guide name notes)
https://www.msrailroads.com/NJ&C.htm

Rowland, Encyclopedia of Mississippi History vol. II (https://ldsgenealogy.com/MS/books/Encyclopedia-of-Mississippi-History-Comprising-Sketches-of-Counties-Towns-Events-Institutions-and-Persons-Vol-II-part-61.htm)

segments.note: Second section, Pattison - Hermanville - St. Elmo (Norton) - Carlisle - Carpenter - Utica - Adams - Learned - Oakley - Raymond. [OPEN] START: 1882 is the first CONFIRMED passenger year, not the opening. Weekly Clarion (Jackson), 14 Jun 1882: the NJ&C 'is now in running order from Natchez to Raymond'; Weekly Copiahan, 24 Jun 1882: the Mississippi Press Association rode a special from Natchez to within 3.5 mi of Raymond in cars seating fifty-six. The 1883 Official Guide lists St. Elmo as 'Norton' (branchline 1883G). The section's opening, somewhere between 1879 and June 1882, is not dated; do not move the start earlier without evidence. END: ownership change, sale to the LNO&T 28 Mar 1890; 1890 is drawn on the LNO&T feature so no year is drawn twice. headway_min 720 (two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE: no timetable frequency was read for any era; the 1889 roster (4 coaches, 2 combines) is consistent with one or two round trips a day.

segments.note: The Y&MV (Illinois Central) 'Natchez District' / Natchez branch, Jackson - Raymond - Utica - Hermanville - Harriston - Fayette - Natchez, taken over with the LNO&T in 1892 (start = ownership date, month not established). LOW CONFIDENCE, [OPEN] END: no dated primary passenger evidence for 1892-1939 was found. 1939 is the last year implied by the one secondary statement, chicagorailfan.com: IC passenger trains ran Jackson - Natchez 'until early 1940's' (undated, uncited); collapsed inward to 1939 because an end in 1940 would still be 'early 1940s'. This is NOT a known end - the last passenger year is unknown, somewhere between ~1939 and 30 Sep 1951, when the Feb 1952 Official Guide prints IC Table 80 'Jackson and Natchez' in its FREIGHT SERVICE ONLY section. Do not extend without a dated timetable or discontinuance order. Mixed trains in the 1940s neither found nor ruled out. Freight continued to the ICG's 1979-81 abandonment (Natchez stub to 2005) - context only, not drawn. The Y&MV merged into the Illinois Central proper in 1946, after this span; the repo draws the Y&MV in IC orange. Whether Y&MV Vicksburg - Natchez trains used these rails Harriston - Natchez is not established. headway_min 720 (two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE: no timetable frequency was read for any era; the 1889 roster (4 coaches, 2 combines) is consistent with one or two round trips a day.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the start is the 1892 ownership date, and the end rests only on a secondary undated rail-fan statement bounded by the 1951 freight-only listing; no dated timetable for 1892-1939 was checked. Treat the years and the headway as unverified.
